institutionName: Institut d'études politiques de Paris (Sciences Po)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Courses that fit my interests and an interesting destination.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy. Sciences Po's website can be a bit confusing but there is all the information I needed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an Erasmus coordinator you could contact. There was also a Welcome Programme but with very limited spots and it cost €250. For those who weren't able to participate in the Welcome Programme there was only a 1 hour introduction lecture.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The mentor programme was good but the Welcome lecture was kind of pointless.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It is very hard to find an apartment but easier to find student residencies. I asked Sciences Po and they sent me a list of recommendations. I ended up living at 2 different places because the first was very expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Cité Universitaire. There is a lot of international students and social events.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It is based on a first come first serve principle. Everyone sits ready by the computer when courses become available and quickly pick courses. A very hectic process.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus coordinator explains the procedure.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was lucky that I got courses in my top 10.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Prepare a long list of courses you would like as the other students get priority - exchange students gets whats left, so some may be unavailable by the time it is opened up for exchange students. Check when the course is held as some are on Saturdays.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It really depended on the course. Some were high level, while others (especially the formation commune classes) were more like a BA introductory course.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There is much more focus on participation - presentations and class discussions. Your grade also depends partially on it.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Sustainability of Growth in Developing Countries (6 ECTS)
Development Evaluation Politics and Practice - Special Topics from Africa (6 ECTS)
Theory and Reality of Environmental Economics (formation commune - 4 ECTS)
Narratives, Perceptions and Realities of Contemporary Africa (6 ECTS)
Africa: A New Emerging Frontier in a Post Covid Context (6 ECTS)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sustainability of Growth in Developing Countries because it is taught by Paul Collier, a well-known developmental economics. The course wasn't amazing but it was interesting to hear about his personal experiences consulting governments in Africa.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Thing for the kitchen as the student residency's kitchen was poorly equipped.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was more expensive than expected, both at restaurants and in supermarkets.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything from sports (tennis, dance, etc.) to cultural classes.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't take any, so I don't know.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Take trips to small towns nearby (like Provins). It is free to travel in the Île-de-France region with a Navigo card.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I mostly hung out with international students. Local students already have a network.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language barrier. I was surprised by how many people didn't speak english.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The café culture, brasseries and wine.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Practice a bit of french beforehand, explore France and enjoy Paris.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not that I can think of.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting many interesting people from all over the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Learning french.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
